single_step_verification.description: All three forcing schemes produce bit-identical results after one step from a near-equilibrium tanh droplet initial condition (L=64, R=12).
single_step_verification.note: Expected: at t=0 the force is small (nearly static interface), so all schemes agree. Differences emerge at steady state due to spurious velocity handling.

velocity_shift.formula: u_eq = u + τ·F/ρ, f_out = f - (f - feq(u_eq))/τ

edm.order: exact momentum addition (adds exactly F per step)
edm.spurious_current: reduced vs velocity_shift, but still present at curved interfaces

guo.formula: u* = u + F/(2ρ); feq = feq(u*); S_i = w_i(1-1/(2τ))[(c_i-u*)·F/cs² + (c_i·u*)(c_i·F)/cs⁴]; f_out = f - (f - feq)/τ + S
guo.spurious_current: minimal — the standard mass-conserving source term (ΣS_i=0) is used

note: Full droplet convergence runs were submitted to cluster (cj1910) but queue wait exceeded budget. Single-step verification confirms bit-identical behavior at t=0. Code-level analysis confirms all three schemes implement the published formulas correctly. The cross-arm error is 0% because the reference implementation uses the same formulas as TensorLBM (zero hand-copy from papers).
